<section class="section" style="padding-top:56px"><div class="wrap"><div class="sec-title"><span class="eyebrow">CORE FRAMEWORK I</span><h2>From Higher Rapport to solidifying values: the four processes</h2></div><div class="proc4"><div class="proc"><span class="no">PROCESS 1</span><b>Higher Rapport</b><p>A state of trust, one step beyond rapport, built on educational love. It forms when we go beyond understanding and empathy to ask “How can I help?”, and grows into a relationship where teacher and student grow together.</p></div><div class="proc"><span class="no">PROCESS 2</span><b>Diagnosing with Questions</b><p>Not with blame or assumptions, but with questions and listening, we accurately diagnose the inner thoughts and feelings behind every behavior. Diagnostic skill is a teacher’s expertise.</p></div><div class="proc"><span class="no">PROCESS 3</span><b>Setting Value Standards</b><p>Rather than one-way instruction or lectures, the Three-Step Questioning Method helps students realize and establish the right value standards for themselves.</p></div><div class="proc"><span class="no">PROCESS 4</span><b>Solidifying Value Standards</b><p>Through consistent follow-up, we warmly encourage and support students so their value standards become habits in school life.</p></div></div><div class="note-box">Higher Rapport, which begins with the teacher’s reflection, meets the Three-Step Questioning Method to set right value standards within students. The final destination of the four processes is for the ten universal values to become habits in students’ lives.</div></div></section><section class="section"><div class="wrap"><div class="sec-title"><span class="eyebrow">CORE FRAMEWORK II</span><h2>Instead of lecturing… the Three-Step Questioning Method</h2></div><div class="chev"><div><b>Step 1 · Value Recognition</b><span>Seeing your behavior objectively</span></div><div><b>Step 2 · Clarifying Values</b><span>Realizing why right values matter</span></div><div><b>Step 3 · Applying Values</b><span>A voluntary commitment to act</span></div></div><div class="qstage"><div><h3><span class="n">1</span>Step 1: Value Recognition</h3><p class="purpose"><b>Purpose</b>Help students look at their behavior or the current problem objectively, without feeling resentful.</p><ul><li>“Was there a reason you said that?”</li><li>“Was there a reason you did that?”</li><li>“Why do you think that happened?”</li><li>“Why did you feel that way?”</li></ul></div><div class="tip"><b>Teacher’s mindset tip</b><p>Don’t point out faults or question like an interrogation. Ask with a genuine wish to help, so the student can answer honestly without shrinking back.</p></div></div><div class="qstage"><div><h3><span class="n">2</span>Step 2: Clarifying Value Standards<small>Let them judge → Ask back → Sum up the value</small></h3><p class="purpose"><b>Purpose</b>Help students find for themselves why right value standards matter and how their behavior affects others.</p><ul><li>“Is that right, or not right?”</li><li>“If you say that, will your friends trust you or not?”</li><li>“If you act that way, will your friends like it or dislike it?”</li><li>“If you speak or act that way, will anyone like you for it?”</li></ul></div><div class="tip"><b>Teacher’s mindset tip</b><p>Don’t rush if the student hesitates or doesn’t give the expected answer. Ask again with follow-up questions and wait until they find the answer themselves.</p></div></div><div class="qstage"><div><h3><span class="n">3</span>Step 3: Applying Values</h3><p class="purpose"><b>Purpose</b>The student chooses for themselves how to apply the right value in daily life.</p><ul><li>“So what would be good to do from now on?”</li><li>“What could you practice to do that?”</li><li>“Then what do you need to do?”</li></ul></div><div class="tip"><b>Teacher’s mindset tip</b><p>Instead of explaining and deciding for them, ask so the student chooses. Truly respect the child’s choice, and warmly encourage even small commitments.</p></div></div></div></section><section class="section"><div class="wrap"><div class="sec-title"><span class="eyebrow">THE TEN VALUES</span><h2>Ten universal values schools should emphasize</h2><p>Values that human conscience recognizes as good regardless of race, religion or nationality: the common ground found in the two authors’ 34 and 22 years of teaching.</p></div><div class="values10"><div class="val"><span class="n">01</span><b>Honesty</b><p>Not lying and not deceiving</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">02</span><b>Sincerity</b><p>Steadiness: putting your heart into something and practicing it again and again</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">03</span><b>Diligence</b><p>Doing whatever comes your way without putting it off</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">04</span><b>Consideration</b><p>A heart and actions that put others at ease</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">05</span><b>Understanding</b><p>Accepting others’ differences and circumstances with an open heart</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">06</span><b>Forgiveness</b><p>No longer hating or resenting others for their wrongs</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">07</span><b>Love</b><p>A heart and actions that help and care for others</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">08</span><b>Positivity</b><p>The mindset that says “I can do it!”</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">09</span><b>Proactivity</b><p>The decision to say “I will,” and the ability to act on it</p></div><div class="val"><span class="n">10</span><b>Truthfulness</b><p>A sincere heart without falsehood that embraces all the values above</p></div></div></div></section><section class="wrap"><div class="contact-band" id="contact">
